run_metadata.coverage_summary: All source tiers were attempted (Tier 1 Commonwealth + all states/territories; Tier 2 councils/GBEs/universities/health; Tier 3 private-sector e-sourcing hubs and major-buyer portals; plus a source-discovery sweep). Connectivity was re-tested at the start of the run: both WebFetch and a direct curl returned a hard organisation egress denial (403 'CONNECT tunnel failed' / EGRESS_BLOCKED) for EVERY external host, including a neutral control fetch to en.wikipedia.org. The agent-proxy status endpoint confirms enabled=true, bundleCoversEveryHost=true and recentRelayFailures listing connect_rejected (connection rejected by organization policy) for the test hosts. This is the SAME session-wide deny-by-default egress block seen on the 2026-09-30, 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02 runs - now four consecutive days. Per the proxy README this is an organization policy denial that must be reported, not routed around. WebSearch still works (it routes through the Anthropic API, not the egress proxy) and was used for a source-discovery sweep across Tier 1-3. Because the spec's fidelity rule requires every tender detail to be taken from the actual notice or its documents, and no notice page could be opened or verified, NO opportunity could be confirmed - so this run records ZERO tenders rather than repeating unverified aggregator snippets. The source-discovery sweep surfaced two buyer-originated public-sector procurement pages not present in any prior run (SA Health procurement/supplier information and the DFAT Development Procurement Pipeline); both are recorded in discovered_sources at medium confidence with a clear note that they were surfaced via WebSearch and could NOT be fetch-verified this run due to the egress block. No tenders, deliverables, dates, contacts, or corporate opportunities were invented.
gaps: Session-wide organisation egress block (4th consecutive day): WebFetch returns EGRESS_BLOCKED and direct curl returns '403 CONNECT tunnel failed / connect_rejected' for every external host, including a neutral control (en.wikipedia.org). No external website could be opened.

Tier 1 (AusTender, NSW eTendering/buy.nsw, Buying for Victoria, QTenders/supply.qld, Tenders WA, Tenders SA, Tenders Tasmania, NT QTOL, ACT Tenders): attempted but UNREACHABLE - every notice/detail page blocked by egress policy; zero tenders could be verified.
Tier 2 (councils via VendorPanel, GBEs/government-owned corporations, universities/TAFEs, public health): attempted via WebSearch only; no detail page could be fetched to verify an opportunity.

Tier 3 (SAP Ariba Discovery, Coupa/Jaggaer/GEP/Ivalua, RangeMe, and major-buyer portals BHP/Rio Tinto/Woodside/Woolworths/Coles etc.): attempted via WebSearch only; all portals remain unreachable for fetch. No corporate opportunity could be verified; none invented. Login/registration-gated corporate RFx remain out of scope as per spec.
Detail/deliverables extraction: not possible for any opportunity this run because no notice or tender document could be opened.

Proxy status checked (curl http://127.0.0.1:45403/__agentproxy/status): enabled=true, selective=false, no external tender domains permitted - consistent with an allowlist that admits only infrastructure hosts (Anthropic API, package registries). This is an environment/configuration issue, not a transient network error, and has persisted for four days.
recommended_seed_additions: SA Health - Procurement and Supply Chain Management / Supplier information (https://www.sahealth.sa.gov.au/.../tenders+and+contracts/procurement+and+supply+chain+management+supplier+information) - SA public-health buyer-originated procurement page.

DFAT Development Procurement Pipeline (https://www.dfat.gov.au/about-us/business-opportunities/development-procurement-pipeline) - Commonwealth forward pipeline of upcoming aid/development procurement, distinct from the AusConnect portal already tracked.

ENVIRONMENT FIX (highest priority): the daily routine cannot fulfil its core mission while the egress proxy blocks all external hosts. Allowlist the Tier 1 government tender domains (tenders.gov.au, tenders.nsw.gov.au, buy.nsw.gov.au, tenders.vic.gov.au/buyingfor.vic.gov.au, qtenders.hpw.qld.gov.au/supply.qld.gov.au, tenders.wa.gov.au, tenders.sa.gov.au, tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au, tenders.act.gov.au), plus vendorpanel.com.au, tenderlink.com and service.ariba.com, so WebFetch can open and verify notices.
